chapter: Pay, the Fletcher Henderson circle and later life
title: Keep Shuffling revue and Eubie Blake
summary: Caldwell was briefly in the Keep Shuffling revue, which ran about two years; Eubie Blake is a fellow lodge member and Caldwell joined the lodge in 1946.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: You know, and I'd forgotten that tune. Very pretty (unintelligible). Well now, let's see. We digressed a little bit. Well, we've got (unintelligible) toured with Keep Shuffling revue, 1927.
Uh-huh. That show -- I forgot who was in that show now.
Well, that was -- was that with Eubie Blake and --

That was Eubie Blake. The big show, wrote "Keep was Keep Shuffling" and the big show was -- that's where he got them tunes. You know the biggest -- Eubie -- Eubie Blake. He's still living. Still makes -- (unintelligible). He makes more money now than he ever did make.
Well, we used --
He went on TV last --
(Simultaneous remarks)
-- play with that group of old timers up in Harlem that Red -- Don Redman used to have?
Right.

Well now, that's ten years ago, and he came out and played "Memories of You," and Don said to me afterwards, well, of course, he can't play it as he used to because he's got arthritis. And ten years later he's got
over his arthritis.
And he's remarkable. He's in his 90's. He's remarkable.
He sure is.
He's a member of my lodge, the lodge I belong to. We belong to the same lodge.
Oh, he does?
Yeah, and W. C. Handy before he passed, Jimmy Rushing Sid Catlett Russian, Syd Catlett, all them fellows. This is known as a (unintelligible) musicians' lodge.
Well, when did you get into masonry?
Oh, well, we better come to that. We'll come to that. Well, how long were you with this keep Shuffling revue?
That -- you know, that thing didn't stay too long downtown, you know.
Oh, it didn't?
Not too long. It stayed about two years, I think.
Well then, did you go out on tour with it?
Once. I think I got far as Cleveland. I got back to New York.
Oh, you didn't stay with him?
No, I didn't stay.
